reason: The finding checks out (06:04Z). CONTEXT.md (2074 lines) has no clause on when an [OK] counts. grep for 'late ok', 'ok timing', 'OK.*post-hoc' and 'user decision after' finds nothing, and the OK REQUEST entry (l.2049-2051) says nothing about a late reply. The principle exists only in round4/REPORT.md section 1.2 and WATCHLIST W45 ('log its time against the first #37/#38 result times; an OK given after a visible score is post-hoc'). The round-5 ok_message_ru (round5/report.json l.19) already asked the user to answer before the first score, so the rule matches what the user was told; only the consequence of a late answer is missing. The gap is still fixable before any score: poll.log's last header is 05:53:56Z, both 56563521 and 56563534 are PENDING, and HEAD 2f6ec9d == origin/main. Feasibility is trivial: text only, no kernel, no mechanism, nothing new under R8, and it only tightens R1-R10 and the READ TABLE. The split between score-dependent items (floor, row 2 F2 = K2, K1 in rows 4/C4) and event items (C2(a) resubmit, row 1/C2(c) K1, K2'' after the trigger) is correct. Round 6's own R6H-2 W1 proposes the same rule but gates floor, row 2 and C4 on 'the LATER of K2 and twin'. That is anti-conservative, because the twin's 0.952 alone reveals the floor outcome. PC6-01's 'first score of any file the item reads' is the right gate, so merge the two using PC6-01's gate. Two weaknesses need fixing, but they do not refute the finding. (1) A poll.log header lags the Kaggle Submissions page by up to ~10 min (+210 s on a failed CLI attempt), and the user (UTC+3, waking ~09-10 local) may look at the page directly. So 'earlier than the first header showing a score' is slightly anti-conservative; the reference point should be the last header where every file the item reads was still PENDING. (2) A CONTEXT rule cannot take away the user's authority. A late OK should be logged as 'user decision after score (post-hoc)'. The strict [bracketed] text stays the recommendation, and the user's explicit override is recorded, not treated as pre-registered. Value is process integrity rather than score. The floor case needs row 3, a twin at exactly 0.952 and a late OK, so the direct score effect is <=~1e-4 either way. That is what team D: Discipline is for, and it is cheap.
fix: Before the first #37/#38 result (earliest ~06:15-06:30Z), append to CONTEXT and commit+push as the user (no Co-Authored-By): 'OK TIMING (pre-score, <hh:mm>Z; merges round-6 PC6-01 and R6H-2 W1): on receipt of the user's reply, the main session runs date -u and logs the UTC time in CONTEXT. A score-dependent [OK] item counts as pre-registered only if that time is <= the last poll.log header in which every file the item reads was still PENDING. Floor 0.952 reads the twin; row-2 F2 = K2 and K1 in rows 4/C4 read K2 or the twin, whichever scores first. Otherwise the [bracketed] strict text is the rule's answer. If the user still chooses the [OK] option, it is logged as USER DECISION AFTER SCORE (post-hoc), never as pre-registered. Event items (C2(a) K2 resubmit, a twin Kaggle Error resubmit, row 1/C2(c) K1, K2'' after the V3 trigger) may be OK'd after their event. The OK request already asked for a reply before the first score.' At the first result, commit poll.log and ledger.md in the same step, so the header times are in git. Do not touch the poller (PID 20052) or the clean-proof job.
realistic_gain: Score EV ~0 (<=~1e-4; only the row-3 twin=0.952 floor case with a late OK, or K1 in rows 4/C4, is affected, P ~0.05-0.15 x P(late OK) ~0.3-0.5).
